newsitem.title: UK: rate rise inevitable - British Chambers of Commerce.
newsitem.headline: rate rise inevitable - British Chambers of Commerce.

text.p: The British Chambers of Commerce said Thursday's interest rate rise was inevitable after a budget which did not choke off consumer demand.
"This increase is the inevitable consequence of a budget which made inadequate use of fiscal measures to subdue consumer demand," said BCC deputy-director general Ian Peters.
"We are witnessing the results of a budget in which political expediency took precedence over the country's economic well-being."
Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown tightened fiscal policy by almost six billion pounds in his first budget but little of that was directed at the consumer.

"Our concern is that further rate rises will be necessary in the coming months, giving greater strength to sterling," Peters said. "This will cause further reduction in export earnings, thus damaging competitiveness, profitability, investment and jobs." -- Mike Peacock, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7708
